chapter: Decca records, the Savoy and Moe Gale
title: Getting Al Hibbler to join the band
summary: The telegram and ticket to Hibbler were intercepted by his girlfriend; McShann finally reached him through a friend and brought him to Kansas City.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yes, and so we come on back, you know, came on back to Kansas City. But in the meantime, I had been down in Texas and had run into [AH] Hibler and had promised Hibler when we leave that we're going to have him join the band. But what had happened, I had sent Hibler

his telegram and his ticket, but his girlfriend would always intercept the ticket -- I mean, intercept the telegram. So Hibler would never get the telegram. So my mother's brother passed, he died. So after he died, I had to go to Oklahoma to the funeral and so I got to thinking, I says, -- no, this fella that knew him called Hibler up. Hibler had left San Anton and went to Fort Worth. He says, "Hibler, McShann's been trying to get in touch with you. Why don't you call him and let him know where you're at?"

Well, in the meantime, Hibler called Kansas City and Kansas City called me in Oklahoma. They says -- and then I got in touch with Hibler. So Hibler says, "Man, I just found out. That girl's been intercepting the telegrams. And I done give up and I says you done give me a dirty deal." I says, "Well, no. Can you get out of there now?" He says, "Yeah, I can get out of here in the morning." I says, "Well, all right, look here, I'll get some money to you tonight. You get out of there in the morning and come on in and I'll meet you here in Muskogee and then we'll drive on up to Kansas City."

So there we were. I got Hibler and Walter Brown. And Walter Brown's thing was just one of them quick things that we got together on, because the other blues and things that we did, we did after he joined, after "Confessing the Blues."
Well, were you going to have Hibler
sing the blues or were you going to have --

No, I wanted Walter Brown to sing the blue, but Hibbler could sing the blues, a lot of people didn't know that. Hibbler was a good blues singer, but after hearing Hibbler sing tunes like I Understand and things like that, the first time that I heard him, I says well, I'll keep him on that stuff and --
So you could afford to pay two singers, Jay.
Well, I guess I was greedy like this. Anything musically I liked I liked it and I wanted it.
You were doing fairly well then, weren't you.

Well, wasn't making no heck of a lot of money because it didn't make no -- well, at that point in life I wasn't worried about trying to make any money. I just wanted to see the thing go, and in fact, I think everybody was making more money than I was. You know what I mean.

We was being booked by -- well, Johnny Tomino in Consolidated but then after we got ready to go east, then Moe Gail started booking us, and so all of this was put together real quick, just like the big band, see, the big band was put together, boom, quick and all of this was one of those quick things.
